organizations.name: Maktab al-Khidamat
organizations.notes: Peshawar-based NGO founded 1985 to recruit and move volunteers to the Afghan war; appears to play a key role in facilitating training and travel of Islamic extremists; published the magazine Al-Jihad; may sponsor a mujahidin unit in Bosnia.

organizations.name: Al-Kifah center
organizations.notes: Brooklyn, New York branch of the MAK; recruited many of those convicted of the 1993 WTC bombing, per press reports.

organizations.name: Al-Jihad
organizations.notes: MAK magazine; told readers to send $100 to the Emirate's Bank in Peshawar to sponsor a mujahidin in Bosnia; said MAK tried to open a school in Muzzafrabad for Arab volunteers for Kashmir.

organizations.name: Emirate's Bank
organizations.notes: Peshawar bank to which donations for a Bosnian mujahid were directed.

sources_cited: Press reports on the al-Kifah center and WTC bombing
key_claims: Afghanistan and Pakistan remain key training and logistics centers for Sunni Islamic militants, with interrelated overlapping guesthouses and training facilities.
The Peshawar-based MAK appears to play a key role in facilitating training and travel of Islamic extremists.
Many of those convicted of the 1993 WTC bombing were recruited via the MAK-linked al-Kifah center in Brooklyn.
The MAK may be sponsoring a mujahidin unit in Bosnia and tried to attract Arab volunteers for Kashmir.
The network shows growing worldwide reach of Sunni extremist groups, with plots involving individuals from several countries and groups.
